dataset.title: Diversity and Distribution of Freshwater Fish in Mineralized Watersheds of the Agno River Basin, Northern Philippines [Data Collection]

site.coordinateMeaning: Station reference coordinate from article Table 1 and dataset Sampling_sites.csv; not individual capture coordinates and not a waterbody boundary.
site.coordinateReferenceSystem: Not stated in the article table or dataset landing-page metadata reviewed; do not infer a CRS.
site.siteScopeLimit: Only ARB7/Paniqui is assigned to Tarlac. Other Agno stations belong to Benguet or Pangasinan and are excluded from this Central Luzon site review.

methods.samplingReported: Article methods report one fish sampling occasion per season at each site, active electrofishing and seine netting along a 100 m riverbank transect, up to 2 hours per station; representative specimens were preserved and sent to the UP Los Ba?os Museum of Natural History for validation.
methods.taxonomicValidationEvidence: The paper reports validation submission but this review found no voucher catalogue identifiers or individual specimen crosswalk. Independent name-catalog checks validate nomenclature candidates only, not the actual collected fish.
methods.temporalResolution: Dataset count columns are labelled Wet and Dry, but the article methods describe wet July/dry January while repository metadata and CSV filenames assign the seasons oppositely. Retain season labels and counts without mapping either label to a date.

siteEvidence.reconciliation: ARB7 station richness and total abundance agree between article Tables 4/5 and the Fish_count.csv row matrix. The wet/dry label totals also sum to 137; their collection-date mapping is unresolved.

taxonomyReview.identityDecision: No source specimen identity is independently certified by this desk review. Keep source names and name-catalog candidates distinguishable.

conflictsAndCaveats: The article says 23 species and 13 families overall; only the ten ARB7-marked source rows are reviewed here.
Dataset CSV spells Oreochromis mozambicus; article Table 4 and Fig. 2 spell Oreochromis mossambicus. Preserve both source forms and hold the specimen-name linkage as a crosswalk candidate.
The article prints Cyprinus carpio with the apparent author/year typo Linnaues, 1975; preserve it in source transcriptions and separate it from the accepted-name authority.

Article methods say fish sampling was wet-season July and dry-season January, but research-data landing-page metadata and filenames label January wet and July dry. No date-to-season assignment is made for counts.
The abstract gives a Shannon range ending at 1.62 while Table 5 gives ARB7 Shannon 1.74. Diversity indices are not used in this site review.
The point is a sampling-station coordinate only. It is not a fish capture coordinate, verified reach geometry, basin polygon or municipal boundary.
evidenceLimits: This is a 2021-2022 historical, single-station, gear- and effort-bounded study record; it does not establish current presence, absence, abundance beyond sampled counts, catchability, fishing legality, safety, diet or bait advice.
Station ARB7 is Paniqui, Tarlac. Do not assign the full Agno River Basin, its other stations, or other province records to Central Luzon/Tarlac.
Reported ecological and taxonomic results require expert review for public species claims; no voucher-level identity check was performed here.
CC BY 4.0 allows reuse with attribution under its terms; it does not provide legal advice or by itself approve a Bangwit product claim.
nextStep: Continue Central Luzon discovery with locality-resolved Bulacan freshwater records and Aurora/Zambales river locality data. Keep Agno ARB7 separate as a historical Paniqui station, and preserve the source name, season-date, and specimen-identity limits. Central Luzon remains incomplete.
